answer: Continuity-Weighted History Pricing. Each identity’s action fee equals base cost divided by accumulated non-transferable history depth, so fresh identities pay far more per action. An attacker must fund every parallel identity through a slow, cost-heavy warm-up period, making mass creation economically irrational. Old identities form an ivory core that is expensive to fake; new ones stay hollow and pricier to operate. Legitimate users cross the nebula of high early fees once, then benefit from declining marginal costs.
